item.title: Another week in Mukobeko: the State opposes bail for Mundubile and 17 others — and the hearing moves to 28 October with the DPP joined, the Zambian Observer reports
item.description: Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 co-accused came back to the Lusaka High Court on Wednesday 21 October for the constitutional bail hearing that was adjourned on Monday. The State has now filed an affidavit opposing release, arguing that treason cases take time and that the Director of Public Prosecutions must be a party. The Zambian Observer reports that both sides agreed to join Gilbert Phiri and that the hearing now goes to 28 October. The 18 remain in custody in Kabwe.

item.title: One name, two sets of minutes: the Speaker recognises Ezra Tembo as Leader of the Opposition and ends the Kampyongo claim
item.description: Speaker Nelly Mutti told the National Assembly on Tuesday 20 October that she had received communication from the NRPUP’s secretary general confirming party president Ezra Tembo as Leader of the Opposition, with Milenge MP Gystave Chonde as Whip and Nyimba North MP Paul Lungu as Deputy Whip. The ruling closes a three-week dispute in which a rival caucus said it had elected Shiwang’andu MP Stephen Kampyongo to the post.

item.title: ‘A fugitive does not acquire immunity by crossing a border’: State House answers the civil-society groups questioning how Jay Jay Banda was brought home
item.description: A coalition of civil-society organisations has asked the Zambian and Mozambican governments to account for the cross-border apprehension of former Petauke Central MP Emmanuel ‘Jay Jay’ Banda and to explain how he came to be in a critical condition at Maina Soko Military Hospital. State House, through Clayson Hamasaka, calls the statement a political booby trap and says only bogus organisations could question the arrest of a man who, it says, publicly called for the President’s assassination.

item.title: K626 million in mining penalties never collected, K3.56 billion owed by the Ministry of Health: the Auditor-General’s account of 2025
item.description: The Auditor-General’s report on the accounts for the year to 31 December 2025, released by Acting Auditor-General Patricia Malaila, finds that the Ministry of Mines failed to collect K626.64 million in penalties from licence holders, that the Ministry of Health carries K3.56 billion in unpaid obligations some dating to 2014, and that only 27 of 5,595 confiscated mukula logs could be found. Unresolved findings fell from 33 to 27.

item.title: ‘Use it or lose it’, then a regional pitch: Botswana and the DRC bring proposals to the Mining Insaka after Hichilema’s warning to licence-holders
item.description: On the second day of the Zambia Mining and Investment Insaka at Mulungushi, Botswana’s minerals minister Bogolo Kenewendo and the DRC’s mines minister Louis Watum Kabamba urged shared processing, equipment manufacturing and border and rail cooperation, with a proposed Botswana–Zambia industrial campus tied to a 300 MW solar project. A day earlier President Hichilema told more than 1,300 delegates that tenements must be explored, that the state has spent almost US$100 million on a nationwide geophysical survey, and that the Insaka ‘is not a holiday’.

item.title: Every director sent home: the new ZEMA board orders a 60-day competency audit and installs an interim chief from UNZA
item.description: Green Economy and Environment Minister Gilbert Siame announced on Tuesday 20 October that the newly constituted board of the Zambia Environmental Management Agency has placed all of the agency’s directors on administrative leave pending assessments of competence and suitability, and appointed Dr Joel Kabika of the University of Zambia as interim director-general for six months. A policy institute has asked for due process and a clear line between the board and management.

item.title: Six days without a court date: Lima MP Kelvin Kaunda applies for bail from Mwembeshi after a transfer his lawyer says he was not told about
item.description: Kelvin Kaunda, the NRPUP MP for Lima, was arrested on 15 October on a charge of assault occasioning actual bodily harm over an incident during the August campaign. He has applied for bail, saying he has been held without being taken before a court; the Correctional Service confirms he has been moved from Lubwa police station to Mwembeshi remand, where his lawyer says he was refused access. His election petition hearing was adjourned on Tuesday because he was not in court.

item.title: A summit by video on Wednesday and one in Harare on Thursday: Hichilema’s two days of regional business, and the message he gave the Great Lakes
item.description: President Hichilema was due to join an extraordinary SADC summit held virtually on Wednesday 21 October to fill treaty positions and elect the next chair of the Organ on Politics, Defence and Security, Foreign Minister Mulambo Haimbe said, before travelling to Harare for the 25th COMESA summit on Thursday 22 October, where Zimbabwe takes the chair from Kenya. On Monday he told a Great Lakes ministerial meeting that hungry populations are hard to govern and that the region should trade food rather than post soldiers.

item.title: ‘A must-win for us’: the Copper Princesses face Venezuela in Rabat tonight after the 5–0 to Japan — and Ken Sekeletu keeps his belt in Tenerife
item.description: Zambia’s under-17 women play Venezuela at 20:00 CAT on Wednesday 21 October in their second Group D match at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, after losing 5–0 to Japan on the opening day. Both sides are without a point; coach Carol Kanyemba says one defeat is not the end of the tournament and captain Taonga Mubanga has promised a win. In Spain, Ken Sekeletu retained his featherweight title with a third-round stoppage.

item.title: From Matero to the launch stage: Olivia Tutu’s memoir ‘Authentic: A Life Chosen, Not Given’ is launched in Lusaka
item.description: Olivia Tutu, the 26-year-old founder of Youth on Sustainable Development, launched her ten-chapter memoir in Lusaka on Saturday 17 October, with Absa Bank chief executive Mizinga Melu as guest of honour and UNDP resident representative James Wakiaga among the speakers. The book was published in August and is expected on Amazon in January 2027.

item.title: ‘No jurisdiction’: Solwezi sends the Mundubile and Zulu sedition case to the High Court — and the question of a Lusaka hearing is left for the judges
item.description: Principal Resident Magistrate Mambwe Mukonde ruled on Tuesday 13 October that the Solwezi Magistrates’ Court cannot hear the two-count sedition case against Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu, and referred it to the High Court. The State had not disputed the defence’s claim that the alleged offences took place in Lusaka. No High Court date has been set, the two men have still not taken plea, and the separate treason matter is untouched. In Lusaka, a bench warrant was issued for Binwell Mpundu in his own sedition case.

item.title: A scuffle on the Supreme Court steps: the Chief Justice tightens security after Davies Mwila is pushed to the ground — and the UPND condemns the attack while disputing the blame
item.description: Former PF secretary-general Davies Mwila was pushed to the ground outside the Supreme Court on Tuesday 13 October after a hearing in the Lima election petition. Chief Justice Mumba Malila called it an attack on the administration of justice and said security had been heightened. The UPND condemned the assault and dared a PF-Pamodzi youth official who blamed its cadres to produce evidence. Police have named no suspects.

item.title: A seat without a contest: Zambia joins the UN Human Rights Council for 2027–2029 — as Human Rights Watch calls the uncontested vote ‘a mockery’
item.description: The UN General Assembly elected Zambia to the 47-member Human Rights Council on Tuesday 13 October, alongside Ghana, Nigeria and Burundi for Africa. Foreign Minister Mulambo Haimbe called it a milestone and thanked the states that backed the bid. Every regional group had put forward exactly as many candidates as seats, for the second year running, and Human Rights Watch said that made the word ‘election’ a mockery.

item.title: The steepest fall in the region — and the heaviest interest bill: Moody’s on Zambia’s debt, as Musokotwane takes the case to Bangkok
item.description: Moody’s projects that Zambia and Ethiopia will record the largest reductions in government debt in sub-Saharan Africa, and lists Zambia among eight countries with a positive outlook — while also forecasting that about 35 percent of its revenue will go on interest in 2027, the heaviest burden in the region alongside Kenya. State House called the projection the result of ‘hard choices’. The Finance Minister is now at the IMF–World Bank meetings in Bangkok, where he spoke for African borrowers on Tuesday.

item.title: ‘Not reduced’: State House says CDF stays at K40 million and only the disbursements have changed — as the Treasury releases K806 million for schools
item.description: After the Finance Minister said next year’s Constituency Development Fund would fall below budget, State House said the allocation ‘has not been reduced and remains at 40 million kwacha per constituency’, with disbursements realigned to need and absorption. NRPUP’s Stephen Kampyongo says any cut will leave MPs unable to meet expectations the Government itself raised. Separately, the Treasury released K806.1 million in fourth-quarter school grants, completing more than K2.3 billion for 2026.

item.title: A truce over the tax ledger: ZRA halts penalties, certificate suspensions and debt recovery while migrated records are reconciled
item.description: After moving years of historical tax transactions from retired systems onto TaxOnline, the Zambia Revenue Authority says it will not impose penalties, suspend Tax Clearance Certificates or pursue debt recovery over unreconciled historical data while taxpayers check their accounts. Business associations had raised concerns about suspended certificates and the reliability of the migrated records. A technical working group has been set up; no end date for the reconciliation period has been given.

item.title: Back to their stations: the Ministry of Health sends 123 headquarters officers to their posts and orders a qualifications audit — as ZAMMSA starts hiring again
item.description: An internal assessment found 123 officers working at the Ministry of Health’s Lusaka headquarters under temporary arrangements, outside an approved establishment of 403 positions. Health Minister Roma Chilengi says they are being redirected to their substantive stations and that everyone left at headquarters will be assessed against professional benchmarks. ZAMMSA, whose entire workforce was dismissed, has advertised eight senior posts, and the Ministry says it is seeking cheaper financing for the sector.

item.title: ‘A matter concerning an individual’: the Government says clergy facing serious allegations should step aside — and the Green Party says the calls on Archbishop Banda are premature
item.description: Information Permanent Secretary Thabo Kawana, in a statement that named no cleric, said it was advisable for clergy facing serious allegations to step aside while the facts are established, and that a case against an individual is not an attack on the Church. The statement follows the arrest of Lusaka Archbishop Alick Banda, who is contesting a charge in court. Two MPs say he should not preside at Mass meanwhile; Green Party leader Peter Sinkamba says resignation calls are premature and politically motivated.

item.title: Four goals and the road to Los Angeles reopens: the Copper Queens beat Uganda 4–1 in Ndola to go through 5–3 on aggregate — Ghana next, in February
item.description: Trailing 2–1 from Kampala, Zambia needed a performance at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium on Tuesday 13 October and produced one: Natasha Nanyangwe and Eneless Phiri scored inside 20 minutes, and Barbra Banda added two after the break for a 4–1 win and a 5–3 aggregate. Sylvia Kabene’s equaliser was Uganda’s only reply. The third round of the 2028 Olympic qualifiers brings Ghana, 10–0 aggregate winners over Mauritius, in February 2027.

item.title: A winning start in Rabat: Zambia’s futsal side beat Libya 3–1 at the Africa Cup of Nations — the hosts, Morocco, are next
item.description: Royd Chishala scored in the second minute and Patrick Mwila added two as Zambia opened their fourth Futsal Africa Cup of Nations with a 3–1 win over Libya in Rabat on Monday 12 October. Mohammed Abu Raas pulled one back late on. Andrea Cristoforetti’s side, who went out in the group stage in 2024, now face hosts Morocco on Wednesday 14 October and Algeria on Friday 16 October.

item.title: The bill for the maize: next year's CDF will be cut as the Treasury counts the cost of a bigger harvest
item.description: Finance Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane says the 2027 Constituency Development Fund allocation will fall below what was initially budgeted, as the Treasury moves to contain this year's overspend — heavier-than-planned maize purchases chief among it. The Food Reserve Agency has been told to expect no Treasury money next season, and road funding is also under pressure.

item.title: 'A criminal matter, not a barrier to reconciliation': State House answers the camp that says there is no peace without release
item.description: State House has rejected claims that President Hichilema's call for national reconciliation cannot succeed while Brian Mundubile remains in detention. Political Advisor Levy Ngoma says reducing the incarceration to a political issue is misplaced because Mr Mundubile is accused of committing a crime. The opposition reads the same moment very differently.

item.title: Food stopped at the prison gate: Sikota appeals to the President as the treason detainees' clock reaches 51 days
item.description: Senior counsel Sakwiba Sikota says food parcels sent by the families of the 18 treason detainees through the Anglican Cathedral were confiscated at Mukobeko's gate, as Chapter One Foundation tells the DPP that the seriousness of a charge is no answer to detention without judicial oversight. The Correctional Service had not responded.

item.title: 'A requirement of the law, not favouritism': the ECZ answers the PR seats row as Britain's envoy makes the case for opposition
item.description: The Electoral Commission says the NRPUP lost its vacant proportional representation seats by missing the statutory seven-day window for submitting its party list, dismissing Emmanuel Mwamba's collusion claims as untrue and unfounded. The row lands as the British High Commissioner urges that Parliament's opposition be allowed to hold the Executive to account.

item.title: Eleven straight years of dividends — but K346 million lighter: ZCCM-IH declares K183 million for 2025
item.description: ZCCM Investments Holdings has declared a final dividend of about K183 million for the 2025 financial year — down from a record K529 million — after a provision for a legacy legal matter and a stronger kwacha cut the local value of its dollar assets. The state investment arm says investment income rose 40 per cent and its market value has passed US$1 billion.

item.title: 'No country can do it alone': Nalumango presses Great Lakes states on a decade-old promise to clean up the minerals trade
item.description: Opening the ICGLR Council of Ministers Responsible for Mines in Lusaka, Vice President Mutale Nalumango said only five member states have fully implemented the regional certification mechanism adopted in 2010 — and urged coordinated action, information sharing and value addition so that minerals fund peace rather than conflict.

item.title: A thanksgiving in Kalomo: the President puts traditional leaders at the front of the Grow Zambia Agenda
item.description: At the Chuungu traditional ceremony in Chief Chikanta's area, President Hichilema — in a speech delivered on his behalf — said every component of the Grow Zambia Agenda is found in the chiefdoms, asking traditional leaders to take a leading role while guarding the peace that growth depends on.

item.title: 'We gave them too much space': the Copper Queens chase redemption — and a third straight Olympics — against Uganda tonight
item.description: Zambia trail 2-1 from Kampala and must overturn the Crested Cranes at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium at 18:00 to keep a third successive Olympic appearance alive. Interim coach Charles Haalubono has fixed on attitude; Uganda say they have come to complete a double.

item.title: No midweek football: the ZPL shelves every Monday-to-Friday fixture — and Nkana's top clash with NAPSA is the casualty
item.description: The Zambian Premier League has suspended all midweek fixtures across its four divisions until further notice, giving no reason, two days after Nkana and Konkola Blades seized the early Stream A lead. Weekend matches on 17–18 October go ahead as planned — for now.

item.title: A song in the stands: the 'Pe Lampi' chants at Nkana bring a ministry warning, a FAZ threat — and a thermometer
item.description: A section of supporters at Nkana Stadium was reported to have sung the campaign song of the detained opposition figures during Saturday's 4–1 win. By Sunday the Sport Ministry had condemned it, FAZ had cited CAF and FIFA rulebooks, and the ruling party's Copperbelt chairman had called it 'hooliganism dressed in political colours'. Fred M'membe's answer: you cannot cure the fever by smashing the thermometer.

item.title: Election eve in New York: Zambia sells its rule-of-law record to the UN — and lobbies for a rights council seat
item.description: Justice permanent secretary Mwenya Kaela Bwalya told the UN General Assembly's Sixth Committee on Friday that the rule of law remains the bedrock of multilateral cooperation, listing new courts, judges and legal-aid expansion as proof. On the sidelines she lobbied for Zambia's Human Rights Council bid. The election is tomorrow.

item.title: The wait ends tomorrow: Solwezi rules on jurisdiction for Mundubile and Zulu — and the DPP has answered the critics
item.description: Principal Resident Magistrate Mambwe Mukonde will rule on Tuesday 13 October on whether her Solwezi court can hear the sedition case against Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu — and plea could follow. The State does not dispute that the alleged offence happened in Lusaka. Meanwhile, the DPP has a word for the delay critics: Shamwana took eleven months.

item.title: Bracing for El Niño: Siame asks the World Bank to move from plans to investments — the Lobito Corridor on the table
item.description: Green Economy Minister Gilbert Siame received a senior World Bank delegation in Lusaka on Friday with two asks: support for the anticipated El Niño drought — forecasters say half the country is exposed — and accelerated green investment along the Lobito Corridor. The Bank says its response will be timely.

item.title: 'Monthly changes hurt planning': an energy expert backs the fuel-pricing review — and counts the VAT holiday's cost
item.description: Energy expert Johnston Chikwanda says the ERB's monthly price changes leave households and businesses unable to plan, and has welcomed the Government's promised review of the mechanism. But he backs the return of excise duty — the waivers were costing the Treasury — and notes VAT's suspension to December will cost a further US$120 million.

item.title: 'Four, five hours without being attended to must not be heard of': Chilengi puts UTH on notice
item.description: Health Minister Roma Chilengi toured the University Teaching Hospital on Thursday and left with a warning: reports of patients waiting four to five hours for attention should not be heard of, accountability must be clear, and the management improvements already begun must be expedited.

item.title: 'Selection on hunger, not names': Haalubono's promise on the eve of the Uganda decider
item.description: The Copper Queens host Uganda at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium on Tuesday at 18:00, trailing 2–1 from Kampala. Interim coach Charles Haalubono says selection will follow determination, not reputation — and captain Barbra Banda has told the senior players to fight for their places.

item.title: Operation Clear Path's ledger: 45 vendors fined, three City Market traders answer today
item.description: Lusaka City Council says 45 street vendors apprehended with police between 4 and 7 October have appeared before the Fast Track Court and been fined. Three more traders — who have stands in City Market but chose the street — appear before the same court today.

item.title: A night for the craft: MISA's media awards honour the newsroom — five prizes for ZNBC, a haul for the Daily Mail
item.description: The MISA Zambia Platinum and Golden Media Awards gala filled the Mika Convention Center on Friday night. ZNBC took five honours — Mark Ziligone the Golden Media Award for Television, Lucky Phiri overall best male journalist in school health reporting — and the Daily Mail's reporters shared in more than twenty awards given out.

item.title: The Fund says yes in principle: a US$1.47 billion staff-level deal — now come the prior actions
item.description: Zambia and the IMF have reached a staff-level agreement on a 36-month, US$1.472 billion Extended Credit Facility. Board approval and a set of prior actions still stand between Friday's handshake and the first disbursement.

item.title: Bus fares follow the fuel: RTSA approves Friday rises — 7 percent intercity, K3.50 inter-mine, K2 on Lusaka locals
item.description: The Road Transport and Safety Agency has approved higher bus fares across the country with effect from Friday 9 October, three weeks after the fuel pump price jumped by more than K6 a litre.

item.title: 'If you engage in corruption, you are on your own': the President puts the civil service — and MPs' allowances — on notice
item.description: Beyond the growth targets, Friday's address to the 14th National Assembly carried a blunt warning to public servants, a rebuke over parliamentary allowances, and a defence of the anti-corruption drive.

item.title: The day after: Kampyongo welcomes the unity call, Britain backs Grow Zambia — with a caveat on opposition space
item.description: The first responses to Friday's address crossed the aisle and the diplomatic row: an opposition lawmaker preaching peace, a British envoy pledging backing with a condition, and the Vice-President urging the country to move on.

item.title: 'A serious betrayal': Sumaili leads the backlash as the 18 October prayer holiday is folded into 29 December
item.description: A day after the Government moved the National Day of Prayer to a merged December commemoration, the minister who once held the religious-affairs portfolio has condemned the change as a betrayal of Christian believers.

item.title: 'Incompetent': Sikota takes on the DPP over the treason-trial delay — as a constitutional petition gets October dates
item.description: Lead counsel Sakwiba Sikota says blaming investigations for the delay in bringing Brian Mundubile and 17 others to court is incompetent. Meanwhile a constitutional petition over the detentions has been scheduled for late October.

item.title: Forty thousand hires under the US health pact — and RDAZ says the queue should start with those already inside
item.description: The US$1.5 billion health memorandum signed on Thursday carries a plan to recruit 40,000 health workers over five years. The resident doctors say existing staff should come first; the opposition questions the deal itself.

item.title: Ninety-first: the Chipolopolo slip a place in the FIFA rankings — even the Togo win could not hold 90th
item.description: Zambia have fallen one place to 91st in the FIFA/Coca-Cola World Ranking released on Wednesday, the 2-0 win over Togo outweighed by bigger gains elsewhere during the international window.

item.title: Eleven arrests at National Heroes Stadium: a fake cash-giveaway post drew a crowd — and a police warning on disinformation
item.description: Police arrested eleven people at National Heroes Stadium on Friday morning after a false social-media post promising free cash drew a crowd to Gate 1. Officers dispersed the gathering when it refused to leave.

item.title: Grow Zambia day: Hichilema opens the 14th Assembly with a five-year agenda, a unity appeal — and a fuel-tax decision that lands this month
item.description: President Hakainde Hichilema ceremonially opened the First Session of the 14th National Assembly yesterday, telling a transformed chamber that the electorate's verdict was 'unequivocal: continuity, unity, progress and hard and smart work'. The address set out the Grow Zambia agenda for agriculture, mining and energy, restored the excise duty on fuel from this month, and ordered an electric-only fleet for government — while saying nothing, in its circulated text, about the third-term question that had crowded the foyer all week.

item.title: The tax comes back to the pump: excise duty returns this month — with an ERB pricing review, an ethanol blend plan, and an electric-only rule for the government fleet
item.description: President Hichilema told the 14th Assembly that the excise duty on fuel, suspended to shield consumers from global price shocks, is restored from October — the revenue earmarked for free education, CDF, school feeding and social cash transfers. The package pairs the tax with a review of the ERB's monthly pricing mechanism, a firmer TAZAMA open-access regime, a local ethanol blending strategy, and a directive that government institutions will now buy only electric vehicles.

item.title: Hichilema courts the Fund: the IMF mission chief is in Lusaka for a successor programme — and the President is selling Grow Zambia as the framework
item.description: President Hichilema met IMF mission chief Edward Gemayel at State House on Wednesday to discuss a successor economic programme, telling him the completed US$1.3 billion Extended Credit Facility must give way to an arrangement 'complementary to our Grow Zambia Agenda' — the plan his officials price at US$65 billion in annual monetary value. The visit also marked a changing of the guard: resident representative Eric Lautier departs, Reginald Darius arrives.

item.title: Two readings of one signature: the health pact's fine print — US$975 million of Zambian money, a mineral clause decoupled — and M'membe's demand to see all of it
item.description: Forty-eight hours after the US-Zambia health compact was signed at the Ministry of Finance, its architecture is clearer: Washington intends more than US$1.5 billion over five years, Zambia pledges US$975 million in new domestic health spending, co-financing fell from US$243 million to US$154 million, and the minerals question has been formally decoupled — though not settled. Fred M'membe calls the deal padded chains and wants the full text published; the minister says the public already won the argument that mattered.

item.title: Monday in New York: Zambia takes its Human Rights Council bid to the vote — as its own rights record is argued over at home
item.description: The UN General Assembly elects members of the Human Rights Council for 2027–2029 on Monday, and Zambia — the African Union-endorsed candidate — has spent the autumn lobbying for the seat, with Permanent Representative Chola Milambo working the corridors of UNGA 81. The bid lands in the same week the Government publicly rejected UN experts' concerns over the treason and sedition cases against opposition figures, telling the world body to let the courts decide.

item.title: Tuesday at Solwezi: the magistrate rules on jurisdiction for Mundubile and Zulu — and a plea, at last, may follow
item.description: Principal Resident Magistrate Mambwe Mukonde has set Tuesday 13 October to rule on whether the Solwezi Magistrate's Court may hear the sedition case against Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu, who argue the alleged offence happened in Lusaka. The ruling — and the plea it could unlock — is the week's first domino in a legal calendar that still holds an untried treason case against 18 accused.

item.title: The mayor's first week: Chitambala Mwewa takes the chain at the Civic Centre — and Operation Clear Path rolls into the CBD
item.description: Chitambala Mwewa was sworn in and installed as Mayor of Lusaka this week — 47 years after his father became the city's first indigenous Zambian mayor — with a mandate he has already started enforcing: vendors cleared, buses impounded, and phase two of Operation Clear Path aimed at the central business district. His first request from the chair is for the council police: better equipped, he says, or the cleanup will not hold.

item.title: Ninety minutes to save the Olympic road: the Copper Queens regroup in Ndola for Tuesday's decider against Uganda
item.description: The Copper Queens are home, hurt, and one goal down. Thursday's 2-1 defeat at Nakivubo — Prisca Chilufya's early opener cancelled out by Agnes Nabukenya and Sylvia Kabene's second-half header — means Tuesday's second leg at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium is a straight fight for the third round, with Ghana or Mauritius waiting for the winner and Los Angeles 2028 at the end of the road.

item.title: The prayer day moves: church mother bodies merge 18 October with the Christian-nation commemoration — one national event, on 29 December
item.description: Zambia's National Day of Prayer, Fasting, Repentance and Reconciliation — a fixture of 18 October since 2015 — is being merged with the commemoration of the Christian-nation declaration into a single observance on 29 December 2026, under the theme 'National Day of Prayer and Christian Heritage'. The church mother bodies say consolidation enhances rather than diminishes the day; this year, the prayers are asked to happen in the pews, not the stadium.

item.title: Bats, jets and leopard cubs: the travel season ahead — Kasanka's migration confirmed, a new Joburg–Lusaka route, and good news from South Luangwa
item.description: The dry-season ledger is filling in. Everwild has confirmed its Kasanka bushcamp for the 2026 bat migration — guests from 25 October to 1 December, with both the Kasanka Trust and the parks authority on board; FlySafair will fly Johannesburg–Lusaka five times a week from February 2027; Proflight is nearly doubling its Jetstream fleet; and at Sungani in South Luangwa, the leopardess Kuvina has been spotted with not one cub but two.

item.title: Opening day: Hichilema addresses the 14th National Assembly this morning — with a term-limits row in the foyer and a divided country in the gallery
item.description: President Hakainde Hichilema ceremonially opens the First Session of the 14th National Assembly today, his first address to Parliament since re-election, expected to set out the Government's 2026–2027 policy direction on energy, development and free education. Outside the chamber, the week's argument has been about a clause he has not proposed — and about the reconciliation his critics say must come first.

item.title: Lumezi North is decided without a ballot: UPND's Anderson Banda elected unopposed — and Mandevu's opposition ticket changed hands at the desk
item.description: The NRPUP, the only party entitled to file a fresh nomination in Lumezi North, did not do so by Thursday's close — leaving the UPND's Anderson Banda to be declared duly elected without a vote. In Mandevu, the Tonse Pamodzi alliance shifted its backing from Jean Kapata to former Lusaka mayor Daniel Chisenga, who filed on an FDD ticket against the UPND's Adrian Banda.

item.title: 'Not credible': Mbita Chitala indicts the August election — an audit of 13,529 polling stations, and a unity government as the cure
item.description: Zambia Research Foundation director Dr Mbita Chitala, a co-founder of the MMD, has declared the 13 August general election not credible — citing the ECZ's six-hour blackout, the closure of the courts during the presidential petition window, and a claimed variance of more than 800,000 votes — and proposed an eight-pillar reconciliation process culminating in a government of national unity.
